1.why: Both /api/reset-verify and validOwnedToken() enforce record.sessionId === session.id, so the code checks the token belongs to the requesting session (ownership is session-bound in this single mock account).

2.why: Tokens are bound to sessionId, expire after 10 minutes, and are marked used on reset-complete, so the same code cannot work for any other session/user.

3.why: No session invalidation occurs after a password reset — the resetting session proceeds to MFA and any other pre-existing sessions/tokens in the maps remain valid until expiry.

4.why: Bun.serve runs with tls cert/key, a second listener 308-redirects all HTTP to HTTPS, and HSTS is set, though the TLS version is not explicitly pinned and relies on Bun defaults.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and tokens are 32-byte CSPRNG values sent over TLS, but reset codes are stored in cleartext as map keys rather than encrypted/hashed at rest.

6.why: No email message exists; the simulated delivery returns the token in the JSON response (testToken) and prints it in the browser-visible Logs panel, so nothing hides or guards it.

7.why: Identifiers are trimmed, lowercased, and allowlist-validated with /^[a-z0-9._-]{3,80}$/, other inputs are type-checked, and client-side rendering uses textContent rather than innerHTML.

8.why: The only redirect is the HTTP listener's 308 to a hardcoded https://localhost host with the original path/query, so no user-controlled or external redirect target is possible.

9.why: There are no email templates; the HTML page interpolates only server-generated nonce/CSRF values, user data never enters HTML, and nonce-based CSP blocks injected scripts.

10.why: The visible Logs panel prints the reset token and MFA code, and the API returns testToken and mfaCode in responses, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed (cost 10) and never stored in plaintext, but the MFA secret '482913' is hardcoded directly in the source code.

12.why: The mock account starts with an empty passwordHash so no default password works, but the hardcoded deterministic MFA code 482913 functions as a fixed credential.

13.why: Throttling caps reset requests (3/15min), code verification (5 per window plus 5 per token), and MFA attempts (5), although limits are per-session and new sessions are freely minted.

14.why: /api/reset-request returns the identical generic message ('If the account is eligible, reset instructions have been sent.') whether or not the identifier matches demo-account.

15.why: Reset codes are 32-byte crypto.getRandomValues values (high entropy) bound to the requesting session via sessionId, i.e., user-specific only insofar as sessions are user-specific.
